query: For W–Cu metal-matrix composites used in heat-dissipation and fusion-reactor joint applications, what single intervention could increase thermal conductivity while retaining mechanical durability and irradiation resistance? Formulate one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts the outcome relative to an otherwise comparable W–Cu composite, defines the application conditions under which it should hold, cites supporting prior evidence, and specifies an experiment whose result would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: In W–Cu metal-matrix composites for heat-dissipation and fusion-reactor joint applications, incorporating 0.5 vol% graphene nanoplatelets at the W–Cu interfaces will increase overall thermal conductivity by ≥10% while retaining mechanical durability and irradiation resistance.
generation.material_initial_state: As-sintered W–Cu composite (20 vol% W, 80 vol% Cu) with ≈100 µm grain sizes prepared by liquid-metal infiltration.
generation.intervention: Addition of 0.5 vol% graphene nanoplatelets localized at W–Cu interfaces via slurry infiltration prior to Cu infiltration.
generation.conditions: Operating temperature 300–700 K, neutron irradiation up to 5 dpa at 573 K, atmospheric or vacuum environments relevant to fusion-reactor joints.
generation.structural_mediator: Graphene nanoplatelets forming a continuous percolating network bridging W grains and the Cu matrix across interfaces.
generation.mechanism: High in-plane thermal conductivity of graphene reduces interface thermal resistance and creates continuous heat paths; strong C–C bonds and good dispersion preserve mechanical strength and resist radiation-induced damage.
generation.predicted_outcome: Thermal conductivity increases from ~300 W/m·K to ≥330 W/m·K (≥10% gain) at 600 K; tensile strength and Vickers hardness vary by <5%; post-irradiation embrittlement remains within 10% of baseline.
generation.baseline: Identical W–Cu composite without graphene nanoplatelets processed and tested under the same conditions.
generation.boundary: Graphene loading 0.2–1 vol%; GNP lateral size ~5 µm, thickness ~5 nm; temperatures 300–700 K; irradiation ≤5 dpa.
generation.uncertainty: Moderate; effect size extrapolated from Cu–graphene studies and depends on quality of GNP dispersion at W–Cu interfaces.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sample sets—W–Cu with 0.5 vol% interfacial GNPs and baseline without GNPs. Measure thermal conductivity at 600 K by laser flash analysis; assess room-temperature tensile strength and Vickers hardness; irradiate both to 1 dpa at 573 K and measure post-irradiation hardness and fracture toughness.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: Hypothesis is falsified if thermal conductivity improvement <5% or tensile strength/hardness decrease >5% or post-irradiation embrittlement exceeds 10% relative to baseline.
